note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Perform testing and inspection of electrical installations

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before the initial verification of a new two-storey house, which information should the inspector collect?
options: Only the client's receipts for all the materials bought
Approved drawings, panel schedule and device ratings
The builder's programme for the painting and tiling work
The power bills for the last year from the previous owner

questions.stem: What does initial verification confirm about a new installation?
options: It follows the drawings and the NEC and is safe to energise
It was finished by the date written in the builder's contract
The client is happy with where every switch was placed
The cheapest materials allowed were used throughout

questions.stem: Why is a periodic inspection of an older hotel's installation carried out?
options: To redesign it in line with the latest fashion in fittings
To check that the power company's meter reads correctly
To find damage, wear and changes that affect safety
To replace every cable that is more than five years old

questions.stem: Before a periodic inspection of an occupied office, why must the extent and limitations be agreed with the client and written down?
options: So the inspector can leave out any circuit he finds hard
So the client knows how much each test will cost in J$
So the power company can plan when to read the meter
So everyone knows what will and will not be inspected

questions.stem: During a periodic inspection you open a sample of outlets and find several loose terminals. What should you do?
options: Stop sampling, since the rest are likely to be fine
Tighten them and leave them out of the report
Open a bigger sample, as more faults are likely
Record a pass, because loose terminals are not a danger

questions.stem: Which defect can be found only by inspection, and not by the usual dead tests?
options: A break in the grounding conductor of a circuit
An insulation fault between a hot conductor and ground
Hot and neutral reversed at an outlet on a circuit
An outdoor fitting not suited to wet locations

questions.stem: When inspecting a house, where on the incoming metal water pipe do you expect to find the main bonding clamp?
options: At the far end of the pipe, in the last bathroom
As close as practical to its point of entry
Anywhere on the pipe, then painted over to protect it
On a plastic section, where it is easier to reach

questions.stem: What does the IP rating on a light fitting for a pool deck tell the inspector?
options: How well it keeps out solid objects and water
How many watts of lamp it can safely take
Which maker built it and in which country
How long its lamp should last before it burns out

questions.stem: You find 12 AWG (3.3 mm²) conductors protected by a 40 A breaker on a general receptacle circuit. What should you record?
options: Nothing, because a larger breaker trips less often
A pass, as long as the insulation test result is good
An advisory, to be done at the next inspection
A defect: the breaker is too big for the conductors

questions.stem: A distribution board has an empty breaker space with no blank fitted. Why is this recorded as a defect?
options: It lets dust in, which can make the breakers trip
Fingers or tools can reach live parts through the gap
It means the board was bought from the wrong maker
The power company will not read the meter until it is fixed

questions.stem: Which label should an inspector expect at a board fed by both the mains and a standby generator?
options: A warning that the board has more than one supply
A label that gives the generator's purchase price
A notice listing all the electricians' phone numbers
A sign telling users to switch each breaker monthly

questions.stem: When inspecting a house with a standby generator, what must the inspector confirm about the changeover arrangement?
options: The generator is fed in through an outlet with a two-plug lead
The generator is larger than the house's total connected load
It cannot connect the generator and the mains together
The changeover switch is fitted outdoors beside the meter

questions.stem: On a new installation, which tests are done before the supply is connected?
options: Continuity, insulation resistance, polarity and electrode tests
Ground-fault loop impedance and GFCI trip tests on each circuit
Available fault current readings and phase rotation checks at the panel
Functional tests of every switch, isolator and appliance

questions.stem: The cable data gives 10.4 mΩ per metre for a 12 AWG (3.3 mm²) hot conductor plus a 12 AWG grounding conductor. What should the loop resistance be for a 40 m circuit?
A 110 V circuit of 12 AWG (3.3 mm²) is 28 m long and carries 12 A. Its hot and neutral conductors together have 10.4 mΩ per metre of run. What is the voltage drop?
options: About 1.7 V, or 1.6%
About 7.0 V, or 6.4%
About 0.35 V, or 0.3%
About 3.5 V, or 3.2%

questions.stem: A breaker needs 100 A to trip instantly, and the voltage to ground is 110 V. What is the largest loop impedance that still lets it trip instantly?
Why must the effective ground-fault current path have a low impedance?
options: So the insulation resistance reading is as high as possible
So enough current flows to make the breaker trip quickly
So the GFCI trips at a lower leakage current than 4 mA
So the neutral can carry the full load of the circuit

questions.stem: The loop impedance measured at the service is 0.4 Ω, and the voltage to ground is 110 V. What is the available ground-fault current?
Why must the available fault current at a panel be known?
options: To work out how many outlets each circuit may have
To choose the test voltage on the insulation resistance tester
To check that each device can safely interrupt that current
To decide the colour of the cables used in the panel

questions.stem: Three circuits each read 300 MΩ when tested alone. Tested together at the board, they read about 100 MΩ. What does this show?
options: One of the three circuits has developed a ground fault
The tester's battery was going flat during the last test
The panel's main breaker was left open during the test
Nothing is wrong: circuits in parallel read lower

questions.stem: Before an insulation test of a whole board, what should be done with a surge protective device fitted in it?
options: Leave it in place, since it will help to raise the reading
Short it out with a wire link for the length of the test
Disconnect it, or follow the maker's test instructions
Remove its ground wire and leave it disconnected for good

questions.stem: Which of these is a functional test, done once the supply is on?
options: Measuring the insulation resistance of each cable
Measuring hot-plus-grounding loop resistance on each circuit
Testing the ground rod with two test spikes
Operating each switch, isolator and interlock

questions.stem: A plug-in tester is used on a GFCI receptacle in a kitchen. What should happen when the tester's GFCI test button is pressed?
options: Nothing, as the tester only shows wiring faults
The GFCI trips and the outlet goes dead
The GFCI trips only after a full minute
The GFCI trips and then resets by itself

questions.stem: After testing the GFCI and AFCI devices, why is the user shown their TEST buttons?
options: So they can check now and then that the devices trip
So they can reset the breakers whenever one of them trips
So they can measure the leakage on each of the circuits
So they can turn off the whole supply each night

questions.stem: A measured loop impedance is higher than the design allows for the circuit's breaker. What could this mean if a ground fault happens?
options: The breaker will trip much faster than it needs to
The GFCI will trip every time a lamp is switched on
The circuit's insulation reading will be too high
The breaker may not trip fast enough to clear it

questions.stem: What is a correct way to deal with a circuit whose loop impedance is too high for its breaker?
options: Fit a breaker with a higher current rating instead
Check for poor joints; the designer decides the fix
Remove the grounding conductor to stop the readings
Record it as a pass, as long as the circuit works normally

questions.stem: A building has a single ground rod that measures 40 Ω. What does the NEC require?
options: Add a second electrode, as one rod must read 25 Ω or less
Nothing: any reading is accepted for a single rod
Swap the grounding electrode conductor for a much thinner one
Move the rod into dry sand close to the building

questions.stem: On a dead 110/220 V circuit with two hot conductors, a neutral and a ground, which pairs of conductors are insulation-tested?
options: One hot conductor to ground only, as the others are the same
Neutral to ground only, with the hot conductors left floating
Every conductor against every other, including to ground
Hot to hot only, as the ground is already bonded

questions.stem: An electrician adds one outlet to an existing circuit in a house. What must still be done?
options: Test it, record the results and follow the GER's rules
Nothing, since one outlet is too small to need any testing
Only a lamp check, as the circuit was tested before
Send the results to JPS in place of an inspection

questions.stem: What does the licensed electrician's signature on the test record of a new installation confirm?
options: That the client has paid for the work in full and on time
That JPS has agreed the date of connection
That the work was tested and the results are true
That the architect approved the building's colours

questions.stem: During an inspection of an existing building you find a receptacle with live parts that can be touched. How should it be recorded?
options: Advisory, to be dealt with at the next inspection visit
No action needed, as long as it carries a warning label
Must correct, to be put right within a few months
Immediate hazard: make safe now and tell the client

questions.stem: An inspection of an existing building finds one item that must be corrected. What overall result should the report give?
options: Satisfactory, since the other circuits are all fine
Unsatisfactory, until that item has been put right
Satisfactory, as long as the client signs the report
No result, because that circuit was out of scope

questions.stem: What decides the interval to the next periodic inspection that the inspector recommends?
options: The client's choice, based on what they want to spend
The type of use, the condition found and the setting
Always the same: every twenty years for any building
The age of the inspector's own test instruments

questions.stem: In Jamaica, what must be in place before JPS will connect a new installation?
options: Inspection and approval by the GER, and a certificate
A signed note from the electrician that the work is done
The architect's drawings stamped and returned to the client
A letter from the municipal corporation's fire officer

questions.stem: In a busy supermarket, you must isolate circuits that feed freezers and tills. What should you arrange first?
options: Switch off quickly before the staff can object
Tell the staff afterwards which circuits went off
Agree times with the manager so stock and data are safe
Leave those circuits out of the tests without making a note

questions.stem: As lead inspector, you check a trainee's schedule and see the same continuity reading, 0.10 Ω, on circuits of very different lengths. What should you do?
options: Sign it, since a steady figure shows very careful testing
Change some figures so the schedule looks more real
Ask the client whether the figures look right to them
Check the trainee's method and retest a sample yourself

questions.stem: Why does the inspector check a sample of terminations for tightness on a new installation?
options: Tight terminals raise the insulation resistance reading
Loose terminals make the GFCI trip faster than it should
Loose terminals overheat and can start a fire
Tight terminals are needed for the meter to work

questions.stem: Cables pass through a fire-rated wall between a hotel's kitchen and its corridor. What should the inspector check?
options: That the hole has been left open for cooling air
That the cables are painted the same colour as the wall
That the cables pass through near the floor level
That the hole is sealed with suitable fire-stopping

questions.stem: On a hotel roof, PVC conduit carrying cables is in full sun. What should the inspector check?
options: That it is painted black so it absorbs the heat
That it is UV-resistant and properly supported
That it is buried under loose gravel on the roof
That it has no fixings, so it can expand freely

questions.stem: In a hotel bathroom, what does the inspector check about an outlet near the basin?
options: It has GFCI protection and suits a wet area
It is the same colour as the bathroom's wall tiles
It is fitted inside the shower, where it is handy
It is wired on the room's lighting circuit

questions.stem: How should a defect be written up in an inspection report?
options: In a short code that only the inspector himself understands
As a general comment, such as 'the wiring is poor'
Only by word of mouth to the client's cleaner
Clearly: what and where, with its priority and action

questions.stem: The client refuses to let you isolate a circuit with a dangerous defect. What should you do?
options: Isolate it anyway and lock the client out of the board
Explain the danger in writing and record the refusal
Leave without saying anything and send the bill later
Repair it live so that the client does not lose power

questions.stem: A circuit failed its insulation test, and the fault has now been repaired. What must happen next?
options: Repeat the tests on it and record the new results
Copy results from a similar circuit onto the schedule
Switch it on, since the repair must have fixed it
Leave it off the certificate and tell the client

questions.stem: When inspecting a new pump motor circuit, what should the inspector confirm about the overload relay's setting?
options: It is at twice the nameplate current of the motor
It is at its lowest setting, so that it trips often
It is about 115 to 125% of the nameplate current
It is at the highest current rating of the supply cable

questions.stem: At the end of the initial verification of a new clinic, what should the client receive?
options: A spoken promise that everything is in order
The tester's printout of readings and nothing else
The signed test record and the panel schedule
The keys to the inspector's own padlocks

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the conductor, run with the circuit conductors, that carries ground-fault current back to the panel (shortened to EGC)?
A 110 V circuit has a voltage drop of 3.3 V. What percentage of the supply voltage is that?
Using I = V ÷ Z, how many amps of ground-fault current flow if V is 110 V and Z is 0.55 Ω?
What are the parts of the work called that the inspector and client agree will not be covered, such as cables under fixed floors?
Two circuits each read 200 MΩ when tested alone. About how many megohms will they read when tested together?
What does the NEC call the point where the supply conductors enter a building and the main disconnect is fitted?
Which button on a GFCI receptacle lets the user check that it still trips?
What is it called when only a part of the accessories is opened and checked, to stand for all of them?
What is the material called that seals holes where cables pass through a fire-rated wall?
In an IP rating such as IP65, which digit tells you the protection against water: the first or the second?
What is the switch called that stops a standby generator and the mains being connected to the house wiring at the same time?
What is the connection called that joins the grounded neutral and the grounding conductors together at the service?
What name does the NEC use for the largest fault current that could flow at a point in an installation?
accepted: available fault current at the point

shortAnswers.stem: Which document lists the defects found, and the condition of an existing installation, after an inspection?
Which part of the verification uses mainly the eyes to check the installation, without test instruments?

essays.stem: Describe how you would plan the initial verification of a new two-storey house. Include the information you need, the team, the instruments and the order of the work.
essays.modelAnswer: First I collect the information: the approved drawings, the panel schedules, the design data such as conductor sizes (AWG) and breaker ratings, the load calculation and the specification, including any test limits it sets and what the Government Electrical Regulator's inspector will expect. I agree with the builder when the installation will be complete and free of other trades. I choose the team, for example myself as lead with two trainees, and give each a role: inspector, tester and recorder. I check that the instruments are in calibration, in good condition and suited to the work: a voltage tester and proving unit, a low-resistance ohmmeter, a 500 V insulation tester (megger), a ground electrode tester and, for later, a plug-in receptacle tester and a GFCI/AFCI tester. I prepare blank schedules and test record sheets. The order of work is: safe isolation, with lock, tag and a proved tester; visual inspection of the whole installation against the NEC and the drawings; dead tests in order, which are continuity of grounding and bonding conductors, insulation resistance, polarity and the ground electrode; then, only when these pass and the checks before energising are done, a competent person energises and does the live tests and functional checks. Finally I complete the test record, list any defects and hand over.
markingPoints: Collects approved drawings, panel schedules, design data and the specification
Organises the team with clear roles
Checks instruments: calibration, condition, suitability
Gives the correct order: isolation, inspection, dead tests, checks before energising, then live tests by a competent person
Plans the test record, defect list and handover

essays.stem: Describe at least eight things you would check during the visual inspection of a new small hotel's installation, and say why each matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I check that conductors are the right size for their breakers, so the breaker protects the conductors from overheating: for example 14 AWG on 15 A and 12 AWG on 20 A. I check that breakers are the right type and rating, and that GFCI protection is fitted to bathrooms, kitchen counters, outdoor and pool areas, and AFCI protection where the NEC edition in use requires it, because the risk of shock or fire is higher there. I check that fittings in wet or outdoor areas are listed for wet locations and have a suitable enclosure rating. I look for the main bonding jumper at the service and the bonding of metal water piping, close to where it enters, so metal parts cannot rise to a dangerous voltage. I check terminations are tight, with no bare copper showing, because loose joints overheat. I check panels have no open gaps and all covers are fitted, so live parts cannot be touched. I check cables are supported, protected from damage and sun, and kept apart from data cables. I look for fire-stopping where cables pass through fire walls. I check labels: the panel schedule, warning notices and dual-supply labels. I check that switches are in the hot conductor, and that disconnects for equipment such as air-conditioning units are in sight and marked.
markingPoints: Conductor size matches breaker; correct device types and ratings
GFCI/AFCI protection and wet-location fittings in wet or outdoor areas
Main bonding jumper and bonding of metal piping, tight terminations and no access to live parts
Cable support, protection and segregation; fire-stopping
Labels, notices and disconnects, with a reason given for each check

essays.stem: Explain the steps of a periodic inspection of an occupied shop, from agreeing the extent and limitations to issuing the report.
essays.modelAnswer: I meet the shop owner and agree what will be inspected, what will not, such as cables hidden in walls, and the sample size of outlets to open. I write these down as the extent and limitations. I agree times to switch off circuits, so tills, freezers and computers are protected, and I find out about any alterations since the last inspection. I bring any earlier report and the drawings if they exist. On the day, I isolate each part safely: switch off, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. I inspect the panel and a sample of accessories, increasing the sample if I find faults. I do the dead tests on the circuits, then a competent person does the live tests such as loop impedance and the GFCI and AFCI tests. I record every reading. I record each defect with what and where it is, and how serious it is, and I make safe and report at once anything that is an immediate hazard. Finally I give an overall result, recommend a date for the next inspection, sign the report and explain it to the owner.
markingPoints: Agrees and records extent, limitations and sample size
Plans shutdowns with the client and gathers past records
Isolates safely and inspects, enlarging the sample when faults appear
Tests: dead tests, live tests by a competent person, all recorded
Records defects by seriousness, deals with hazards at once, gives overall result, next date and explains the report

essays.stem: A circuit is 30 m long, with a 12 AWG (3.3 mm²) hot conductor and a 12 AWG grounding conductor. The cable data gives 10.4 mΩ per metre for the pair. The loop impedance measured at the panel is 0.35 Ω. The breaker's maker says it trips instantly at 100 A, and the voltage to ground is 110 V. Work out the loop resistance of the circuit, the expected loop impedance at the far end and the ground-fault current, and say whether the circuit is acceptable. Show your working.
essays.modelAnswer: Loop resistance = 30 m × 10.4 mΩ per metre = 312 mΩ, which is 0.312 Ω. The expected loop impedance at the far end = 0.35 + 0.312 = 0.662 Ω. The ground-fault current is I = V ÷ Z = 110 ÷ 0.662 = about 166 A. The breaker needs 100 A to trip instantly, so 166 A is enough, and the largest loop impedance that still gives 100 A is 110 ÷ 100 = 1.1 Ω, which 0.662 Ω is well below. The conductors warm up in a fault and their resistance rises, so a margin is sensible, and here there is a good one. The circuit is acceptable. If the measured loop resistance on site were much higher than 0.312 Ω, I would look for a loose or poor joint before accepting the result.
markingPoints: Loop resistance = 0.312 Ω (about 0.31 Ω)
Expected loop impedance = 0.662 Ω (about 0.66 Ω)
Compares with the 100 A needed, or the 1.1 Ω maximum, and notes the margin for heating
Ground-fault current about 166 A
States the circuit is acceptable and what a higher reading would mean

essays.stem: Explain the three priorities used to record defects in an inspection report on an existing installation: immediate hazard, must correct and advisory. Give an example of each and say what the inspector must do.
essays.modelAnswer: Immediate hazard means someone could be hurt now. An example is a broken receptacle with live parts that can be touched, or a cable with bare conductors in reach. The inspector must tell the person in charge at once, make it safe with their agreement, for example by isolating the circuit, and record it. Must correct means it is not dangerous at this moment but would become so if a fault happened, or it breaks an NEC rule that matters for safety. Examples are a missing grounding conductor to a metal fitting, no GFCI on an outdoor receptacle, or a breaker too large for its conductors. These must be put right urgently. Advisory means the installation does not meet the current code but is not unsafe, for example an old panel directory or a missing label. The client should plan to deal with it. Any immediate hazard or must-correct item makes the overall result unsatisfactory. Each defect is written clearly, with its location and the action needed.
markingPoints: Immediate hazard: correct meaning and example
Action for an immediate hazard: tell the client, make safe, record
Must correct: correct meaning, example and urgent action
Advisory: correct meaning and example
Effect on the overall result and clear recording

essays.stem: Compare initial verification with periodic inspection. Cover the purpose, when each is done, how much is inspected and tested, and the document issued.
essays.modelAnswer: Initial verification is done on a new installation, or a new addition, before it is put into use. Its purpose is to prove that the work follows the approved drawings and the NEC and is safe to energise. Every circuit is inspected and fully tested: continuity of grounding conductors, insulation resistance, polarity and electrode resistance while dead, then the checks before energising, loop impedance, available fault current, GFCI and AFCI tests, voltage drop where needed and functional tests by a competent person. The results go on a signed test record, and the installation goes forward for the GER's inspection and approval before JPS connects it. Periodic inspection is done on an existing installation at intervals, or when a building changes hands or use. Its purpose is to find damage, wear, overloading or unsafe alterations. The extent and limitations are agreed first, and a sample of accessories may be opened, with the sample enlarged if faults are found. An inspection report is issued that lists each defect by seriousness, gives an overall result and recommends when the next inspection should be done.
markingPoints: Initial: new work, before use, to confirm drawings, the NEC and safety
Initial: everything inspected and fully tested; signed test record and GER approval before JPS connects
Periodic: existing work, at intervals or change of use, to find deterioration
Periodic: agreed extent and limitations, sampling
Periodic: inspection report with defects by seriousness, overall result and next date

essays.stem: As lead inspector, you supervise two trainees testing a small clinic. Explain how you would organise the work, keep it safe and check their results.
essays.modelAnswer: Before we start, I brief the trainees on the job, the drawings and the order of work, and I give each a clear role, such as tester and recorder, swapping later. I agree with the clinic manager when each circuit can be off, because some equipment may be important to patients. I show them the safe isolation for each circuit: switch off, lock off with their own padlocks, tag and prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after. I check their instruments and leads first. I stay close while they test, especially during insulation tests, so nobody touches a circuit under test. I watch the method on the first circuits and correct mistakes early. When they record readings, I compare them with what I expect: for example, longer circuits should have higher loop resistance. Results that look odd or too neat, I retest myself. Live tests are done only by me or another competent person. At the end I check the whole test record, sign it, and talk through with the trainees what they did well and what to improve.
markingPoints: Briefs the team and gives roles
Plans shutdowns with the client
Ensures safe isolation and checks instruments
Supervises closely and checks results against expectations, retesting doubtful ones
Keeps live tests for a competent person; signs off and gives feedback

essays.stem: Describe what you would check when inspecting a house's standby generator connection and changeover switch, and why each check matters.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check that there is a proper changeover (transfer) switch, and that it cannot connect the generator and the mains at the same time. This stops the generator feeding back into JPS lines, where it could kill a line worker, and stops damage when the mains returns. A generator must never be fed in through an ordinary outlet with a two-plug lead. I check that the changeover switch is rated for the full load current and that its neutral arrangement matches the design, so that the neutral is bonded to ground in one place only. I check that the generator inlet and cable are of the right rating, protected and weatherproof. I check that the generator is grounded as the design, the NEC and the maker require. I check that the generator is placed outdoors, away from doors and windows, because its exhaust gives off carbon monoxide. I check that there are warning labels at the panel saying there is more than one supply, and that the user knows how to change over safely. Finally the circuits are tested on both supplies by a competent person.
markingPoints: Proper changeover switch that prevents parallel connection, with the reason (back-feed danger)
No connection by a two-plug lead through an outlet
Ratings of switch, inlet and cable; weatherproofing; neutral arrangement
Grounding and safe generator position (carbon monoxide)
Labels, user instruction and testing on both supplies

essays.stem: Explain what the main bonding jumper and the bonding of metal piping do, why they are needed, and how you would inspect and test them.
essays.modelAnswer: At the service, the main bonding jumper joins the grounded (neutral) conductor, the grounding conductors and the metal of the service equipment together. The bonding of metal water piping and other metal services joins them to the same system. This is needed because, during a ground fault, metal parts could be at different voltages from each other. A person touching two of them could get a shock. Bonding keeps them at nearly the same voltage, and the bonding jumper gives the fault current a low-impedance path back to the transformer so the breaker trips quickly. To inspect them, I check that the jumper and bonding conductors are of the size the design and the NEC table give, fixed to each pipe near where it enters with a listed clamp on clean metal, and tight at the service panel. I also check that the neutral and ground are joined only at the service, and kept apart in sub-panels. To test, with the installation isolated, I use a low-resistance ohmmeter with nulled leads between the panel's ground bar and each bonding point. The reading should be very low, a small fraction of an ohm, and I record it. In a sub-panel, the neutral bar and ground bar should read open.
markingPoints: Defines the main bonding jumper and bonding of metal piping and what they connect
Explains why: same voltage in a fault and a low-impedance fault path
Inspection: size, position near entry, listed clamp, neutral-ground bond at the service only
Test: low-resistance ohmmeter with nulled leads, installation isolated
Expects a very low reading, open neutral-to-ground in sub-panels, and records results

essays.stem: Explain how the age of an installation, the Jamaican climate and the way a building is used affect what you look for during a periodic inspection. Give examples.
essays.modelAnswer: Older installations may have cable insulation that has gone brittle, few or no GFCI or AFCI devices, missing grounding conductors to lighting points and panels that no longer meet the code. Over the years, owners often add circuits or air-conditioning units without upgrading the supply, so I check for overloading, heat marks and alterations done badly. The climate matters too. Near the coast, salt air corrodes metal boxes, conduit, clamps and terminals, so I look for rust and green corrosion. Strong sun breaks down plastic conduit and cable sheaths outdoors. Heavy rain and flooding let water into outdoor fittings and low boxes. After a hurricane, I look for damaged overhead cables, loose fixings and water in panels. Pests such as rats and termites can damage cables in roofs. The use of the building also matters: a hotel kitchen, a pool area or a workshop is harder on the installation than a quiet office, so I inspect these areas more closely and may recommend a shorter interval to the next inspection.
markingPoints: Age: deteriorated insulation, missing GFCI/AFCI or grounding conductors, out-of-date panels
Alterations and overloading added over time
Climate: salt-air corrosion, sun damage, water entry, hurricane damage
Pests and other local causes of damage
Use of the building affects focus and the next-inspection interval

practical1.title: Inspect and test a training installation bay and complete its certificate
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a training bay wired as a small apartment: a distribution panel with a main bonding jumper and separate neutral and ground bars, a lighting circuit, a 110 V receptacle circuit, a 220 V water-heater circuit, a bathroom GFCI receptacle, a metal water pipe with a bonding clamp, and a ground rod if the Centre has one. The bay is NOT connected to any supply. The assessor has planted defects, such as a breaker too large for its conductors, a missing filler plate in the panel, a fitting not suited to a wet location, a loose bonding clamp and a switch in the neutral. As a group, plan the verification against the approved drawings and the NEC rules the Centre uses, and give each member a role (lead inspector, inspector, tester, recorder), swapping so that everyone tests. Isolate and lock off the bay's supply point with every member's padlock and a tag, and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. Carry out a full visual inspection on the inspection checklist. Then carry out the dead tests: continuity of the bonding conductors and of each grounding conductor (hot plus grounding loop), insulation resistance at the test voltage the assessor sets (typically 500 V), polarity and, if fitted, the ground rod. Work out the expected loop resistance from the cable data given, add the impedance at the panel the assessor gives you, find the ground-fault current and compare it with the current the breaker needs to trip. Complete the test record, marking the live tests (loop impedance, GFCI and AFCI tests) 'to be done by a competent person', and list every defect with the action needed.
materials: Training installation bay with planted defects, not connected to any supply
Low-resistance ohmmeter, insulation tester (megger) and ground electrode tester if a training rod is fitted
Lock-off kit, a padlock for each member and tags
Cable resistance data, the impedance at the panel and the breaker trip currents (from the assessor)
Approved drawing, blank inspection checklist, test record and defect list
Calculators, torch and hand tools for opening accessories

Isolated, locked off and proved dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
Inspected their part of the bay against the checklist and found defects

safety: The bay is never connected to a supply during this task; live tests are only written up, not done
Every member fits their own padlock before any cover is removed

Use only test leads and probes in good condition

practical2.title: Carry out an inspection of an older training installation and write the inspection report
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a training rig as an older shop installation, NOT connected to any supply, with signs of wear and alterations: a corroded box, a cracked receptacle, an added air-conditioning circuit with an oversize breaker, a missing panel directory, an outdoor receptacle with no GFCI protection and a loose terminal. The assessor plays the shop owner. As a group, first meet the 'owner' to agree the extent, the limitations and the sample of accessories to open, and write them down. Then isolate and lock off the rig with every member's padlock and a tag, and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. Each member inspects a part of the rig and opens accessories from the sample, enlarging the sample if faults are found. Carry out dead tests on a sample of circuits. The assessor gives a card with the live test results a competent person took (loop impedance, GFCI and AFCI test results): compare them with the limits given. Record every defect as an immediate hazard, a must-correct item or an advisory, with its location and action. Complete the inspection report with an overall result and a recommended date for the next inspection, then present it to the 'owner' and answer their questions.
materials: Training rig set up as an older shop installation, not connected to any supply
Card of live test results and limits (from the assessor)
Voltage tester and proving unit; insulation tester and low-resistance ohmmeter
Lock-off kit, a padlock for each member and tags
Blank agreement sheet for extent and limitations, and a blank inspection report
Hand tools, torch, camera or phone

checklist: Took part in agreeing the extent, limitations and sample
Isolated and proved dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
Inspected their part of the rig and enlarged the sample when faults were found
Recorded each defect they found with the right priority and a sensible action
Compared the live test results with the limits and drew the right conclusions
Helped give the right overall result and next inspection date
Explained findings to the 'owner' clearly and politely
safety: The rig is never connected to a supply during this task
Every member fits their own padlock before any cover is removed
Treat corroded or cracked parts with care: wear gloves and safety glasses
Live tests are not done by trainees: their results come from the assessor's card
